subproblem.title: Lower mass bound at a tangent point: liminf t^{−n} μ_V(B_t(x)) ≥ θ ω_n (eventual form)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N, V an n-varifold on U, x ∈ ℝ^N, T ∈ G(N,n), θ ∈ ℝ with HasTangentPlane V x T θ. Then for every c ∈ [0,∞] with c < ofReal(θ) · ω_n (ω_n = unitBallVolume n) there is δ > 0 such that c · t^n ≤ μ_V(B_t(x)) for all t ∈ (0, δ); i.e. ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ V.weight (closedBall x t).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ → ∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, c < ENNReal.ofReal θ * unitBallVolume n → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), c * ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n ≤ V.weight (closedBall x t)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step (1.3) of the parent proof, in 'eventually' form. Uses the sibling results weight_blowup (Submission.tgc_weight_blowup_tendsto) and plane_ball_measure (Submission.tgc_plane_closedBall_hausdorff). Notation: μ := V.weight; ω := unitBallVolume n; H := μHE[n] on ℝ^N; W := (T.plane : Set ℝ^N); ν := H.restrict W.

1. Finiteness; real numbers. HasTangentPlane V x T θ gives θ > 0. ω = volume(ball(0,1)) in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is finite (measure_ball_lt_top), so a := ofReal θ · ω < ∞, and c < a forces c < ∞. Put c_r := c.toReal and a_r := θ · ω.toReal = a.toReal (ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal). Since c, a < ∞ and c < a, c_r < a_r (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal).

2. Choice of κ. The map κ ↦ a_r κ^n is continuous and equals a_r at κ = 1; hence it tends to a_r > c_r as κ → 1 from the left, so eventually in 𝓝[<] 1 we have c_r < a_r κ^n, and eventually κ ∈ (0,1) (Ioo_mem_nhdsLT). Choose κ with 0 < κ < 1 and c_r < a_r κ^n.

3. A cut-off. Define g(v) := min(1, max(0, (1 − ‖v‖)/(1 − κ))) for v ∈ ℝ^N. g is continuous, 0 ≤ g ≤ 1; if ‖v‖ ≤ κ then (1 − ‖v‖)/(1 − κ) ≥ 1, so g(v) = 1; if ‖v‖ ≥ 1 then (1 − ‖v‖)/(1 − κ) ≤ 0, so g(v) = 0. Thus g vanishes outside the compact set closedBall(0,1) and g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) (HasCompactSupport.intro).

4. Lower bound for the limit value. By plane_ball_measure with r = 1, ν(closedBall(0,1)) = H(W ∩ closedBall(0,1)) = ω < ∞ (Measure.restrict_apply and commutativity of ∩). As g is continuous, |g| ≤ 1 and g = 0 off closedBall(0,1), g is ν-integrable (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded on closedBall(0,1), then integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset). Pointwise 1_{closedBall(0,κ)} ≤ g (g ≥ 0 everywhere, g = 1 on closedBall(0,κ)), and the indicator is ν-integrable because ν(closedBall(0,κ)) = ω · ofReal(κ)^n < ∞ (plane_ball_measure with r = κ ≥ 0). By monotonicity of the integral (integral_mono) and integral_indicator_const:
 ∫_W g dH = ∫ g dν ≥ ν(closedBall(0,κ)).toReal = (ω · ofReal(κ)^n).toReal = ω.toReal · κ^n.
 Multiplying by θ > 0: ℓ := θ ∫_W g dH ≥ a_r κ^n > c_r.

5. Eventually large blow-up integrals. By weight_blowup applied to g, F(t) := t^{−1}^n ∫ g(t^{−1}·(y − x)) dμ(y) → ℓ as t → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0. As ℓ > c_r, eventually F(t) > c_r (Tendsto.eventually with eventually_gt_nhds); also eventually t > 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). Fix such a t; it remains to show c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(closedBall(x,t)).

6. Comparison with the ball mass. If μ(closedBall(x,t)) = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise put h_t(y) := g(t^{−1}·(y − x)). Then 0 ≤ h_t ≤ 1_{closedBall(x,t)}: if y ∉ closedBall(x,t) then ‖t^{−1}(y − x)‖ = ‖y − x‖/t > 1, so h_t(y) = 0; and h_t ≤ 1 everywhere. The indicator is μ-integrable since μ(closedBall(x,t)) < ∞, so by integral_mono_of_nonneg, ∫ h_t dμ ≤ ∫ 1_{closedBall(x,t)} dμ = μ(closedBall(x,t)).toReal. Hence c_r < F(t) ≤ t^{−1}^n · μ(closedBall(x,t)).toReal.

7. Back to [0,∞]. Since c < ∞ and μ(closedBall(x,t)) < ∞: c = ofReal(c_r) and ofReal(t^{−1}^n · μ(closedBall(x,t)).toReal) = ofReal(t^{−1}^n) · μ(closedBall(x,t)) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul with t^{−1}^n ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). As c_r ≥ 0, the strict real inequality of step 6 gives c < ofReal(t^{−1}^n) · μ(closedBall(x,t)) (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff_of_nonneg). Multiplying by ofReal(t)^n and using ofReal(t)^n · ofReal(t^{−1}^n) = ofReal((t·t^{−1})^n) = 1 for t > 0:
 c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ ofReal(t^{−1}^n) · μ(closedBall(x,t)) · ofReal(t)^n = μ(closedBall(x,t)).
 This holds on an 𝓝[>] 0-eventual set of t, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: θ > 0 and ω_n < ∞, so c < θω_n is finite; pick κ ∈ (0,1) with c < θ ω_n κ^n (continuity of κ ↦ κ^n at 1).
θ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n ≥ θ H^n(T.plane ∩ B_κ(0)) = θ ω_n κ^n > c (plane_ball_measure).
weight_blowup: t^{−n}∫ g((y − x)/t) dμ_V → θ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n, hence eventually > c.
t^{−n}∫ g((y − x)/t) dμ_V ≤ t^{−n} μ_V(B_t(x)); multiply back by t^n in [0,∞].
